long_biography.plain_text:
An Atlantic crossing crystallised Swedish entrepreneur Mikael Krafft's idea for Star Clippers: build two passenger vessels modelled on the clippers he had admired as a boy. He spent three years studying preserved nineteenth-century plans and worked with naval architects and engineers before the first new clipper-style passenger ship in decades entered service.

Krafft's fascination began in Saltsjöbaden, near Stockholm, where he helped at Plym's shipyard and listened to stories about the great sailing ships. At ten he sailed his own wooden boat across open water to Åland to explore the museum ship Pommern. Star Clippers later added a five-masted full-rigged ship to its two barquentines, translating that childhood curiosity into a lasting niche within the cruise industry.
